methodological_rigor.justification: This is a double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 randomized clinical trial with 1:1 randomization and stratification (sex and liver metastasis), using independent review committee–assessed PFS per RECIST 1.1 as the primary endpoint. Time-to-event analyses report hazard ratios with CIs from stratified Cox models, and the manuscript addresses treatment switching via supportive crossover-adjusted OS analyses (RPSFTM and 2-stage methods). While the crossover is ethically appropriate, it complicates OS inference and results in wider uncertainty (eg, OS HR 0.73; 95% CI crossing 1.0), keeping the statistical assessment just short of exemplary.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: As an individual randomized, double-blind phase 3 trial in recurrent/metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma, the Oxford LoE is 1b. Endpoints are directly clinically meaningful (PFS and mature OS) with sustained PFS benefit (median 9.6 vs 7.4 months; HR 0.53) and clinically meaningful OS improvement at 3-year follow-up despite crossover. Given the unmet need in this setting and guideline-relevant first-line therapy, the translational and practice relevance is very high.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript states CONSORT adherence and provides core trial elements (sites, dates, eligibility, randomization/stratification, ITT endpoint definitions, and independent data monitoring). Protocol and statistical analysis plan availability are explicitly noted in supplements, and the crossover and its analytic implications are discussed. Data/code sharing is not described as an open repository in the blinded text, but the presence of protocol/SAP improves reproducibility relative to typical reports.

novelty_literature.justification: The main contribution is mature 3-year efficacy and safety follow-up for a PD-1 antibody plus chemotherapy regimen in recurrent/metastatic NPC, along with exploratory gene-expression biomarker analyses. Given that similar PD-1 plus chemotherapy phase 3 trials exist in this disease area, the novelty is mainly long-term durability and biomarker hypothesis generation rather than a wholly new therapeutic concept.

writing_presentation.justification: The abstract is quantitatively detailed (medians, HRs, and AE rates) and clearly communicates the crossover context and supportive OS analyses. Methods are well structured, with definitions of endpoints and analytic approaches, and limitations of crossover adjustment are explicitly acknowledged. Figures and captions (disposition, PFS, OS) provide interpretable summaries in the normalized format.

key_strengths: Double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 RCT with independent review committee–assessed PFS primary endpoint.
Sustained PFS benefit (HR 0.53) and mature OS results with crossover-aware supportive analyses.
Protocol and statistical analysis plan explicitly available in supplements; CONSORT adherence stated.
Exploratory gene-expression profiling suggesting a B-cell signature associated with greater OS benefit.
key_concerns: High crossover rate limits clean between-arm OS interpretation and increases reliance on model-based adjustments.
Biomarker findings are exploratory and require prospective validation; risk of over-interpretation if not framed cautiously.
Generalizability may be region-specific (all sites across Asia) and depends on comparability of standard chemo backbones.
chief_reviewer.rationale: Well-executed pivotal trial update with clinically meaningful durability supports acceptance in a high mid-tier oncology journal; revisions should tighten framing around crossover-adjusted OS and exploratory biomarkers.
